speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you are a newborn presenting with increasing yellow discoloration of the eyes and skin. To begin my assessment, how many weeks old is the baby, and when did you first notice the jaundice?

speaker: Patient
text: 2-week-old female newborn. The patient has been experiencing increasing yellow discoloration of her eyes and skin for 2 days. She was born at 39 weeks' gestation, initially weighed 3066 g and now weighs 3200 g. The patient is exclusively breastfed.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Breastfeeding Jaundice (Physiologic Jaundice exacerbated by insufficient intake).
Based on the history of a 2-week-old exclusively breastfed infant with jaundice appearing after the first week and stable weight gain, this presentation is classic for breastfeeding jaundice due to relative dehydration.
Do you observe fewer than 6 wet diapers per day or any signs of significant fussiness when feeding?
